key_insight: Linearizing the Boltzmann equation with its full collision operator recovers classical incompressible shear-flow stability and transient-growth results within a unified kinetic framework.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables direct comparison of full and simplified collision models for predicting disturbance amplification and instability in canonical shear flows.
method: Discretize full hard-sphere, BGK, ES-BGK and Shakhov operators using a shared, energy-stable formulation.
Combine fast spectral collision evaluation with matrix-free shift-invert Arnoldi and relaxation-model preconditioning.
Compute transient growth, resolvent norms and pseudospectra using a kinetic disturbance-energy norm.
evidence_signal: Across four canonical flows at Reynolds numbers 10²–10⁵, incompressible-limit eigenvalues agree with benchmarks to a few parts in 10⁷ for relaxation models and 10⁶ for the full operator; optimal growth and resolvent norms agree within 0.1%.
watch_item: The four-dimensional kinetic problem remains computationally demanding, and validation reported here concerns canonical flows in the incompressible limit.
paper_title: Kinetic linear stability theory for incompressible parallel shear flows with the full Boltzmann collision operator
